_note: The Countdown page (guide.btownbrief.com/countdown/) renders from this file, in this order — actually it re-sorts by `start`, soonest first, so you can add an entry anywhere. HAND-EDITED. Nothing writes to this file automatically, on purpose: a wrong date here is the one unforgivable error on this site. To add an event: copy a block, give it a unique `id`, and fill in `start` (YYYY-MM-DD, local Burlington date), optional `end` for a multi-day run, optional `time` (24h "HH:MM", only if the start time is firm) with a `timeLabel` for how it should read. `status` must be either "confirmed" — you personally opened a page that states the date, and it is listed in `sources` — or "expected", which means the organiser has not announced it yet: those entries show `window` ("usually the second weekend of September") instead of a ticking clock, and carry a "date not announced yet" tag. Never put a guessed date on a "confirmed" entry; if you are not sure, it is "expected". `start` on an expected entry is used ONLY to place it in the stack and is never shown. `color` is a hue key from countdown.js (lake, maple, coral, foliage, sap, evergreen, twilight, slate, plum, moss); the page reassigns it if two neighbours would clash, so it is a preference, not a promise. `why` is one line, second person, concrete, no hype. An entry drops off the page by itself the day after its `end` (or `start`). Set "hidden": true to pull one without deleting it. When an "expected" entry gets announced, fill in the real dates, flip it to "confirmed", and add the source URL.

events.name: Champlain Valley Fair
events.why: Ten days of the midway, the grandstand and the demolition derby — the last thing standing between you and September.

events.name: South End Art Hop
events.why: Three days when every warehouse, garage and loading dock in the South End opens its doors and hangs art on the wall.

events.name: Pride Vermont Parade & Festival
events.why: The parade comes down Main Street at noon and the whole thing ends up in Battery Park.

events.name: Big Pond Improv Festival
events.why: Three nights of improv teams from all over at the Comedy Club — the one weekend the room runs on nothing but nerve.

events.name: Grand Point North
events.why: Grace Potter's festival on Waterfront Park — three days of music with the lake right behind the stage.

events.name: Green Mountain Book Festival
events.why: A day of Vermont writers at Phoenix Books and the Fletcher Free, ending with the keynote in the library.
events.venue: Phoenix Books & Fletcher Free Library, Burlington

events.name: Vermont Cheesemakers Festival
events.why: Forty-odd Vermont cheesemakers in the Breeding Barn at Shelburne Farms. Come hungry, leave heavier.

events.name: UVM Hockey Home Opener
events.why: Gutterson fills up, the band starts, and winter in Burlington is officially open for business.

events.name: Vermont International Film Festival
events.why: A week of films you will not get another chance to see, most of them at Main Street Landing.

events.name: Vermont Tech Jam
events.why: The state's tech job fair, free and open — go if you are hiring, looking, or just nosy about who is building what.

events.name: Howl'ween Dog Costume Contest
events.why: Church Street hands the marketplace over to dogs in costume. It is exactly as good as it sounds.

events.name: Elf the Musical
events.why: The Flynn's big holiday run. Tickets go early because every family in the county has the same idea.

events.name: Tree Lighting & Santa Parade
events.why: Carollers at five, then 100,000 lights go on at once and downtown is officially in December.

events.name: Holiday Pops
events.why: The Vermont Symphony's holiday night at the Flynn — the one your grandmother asks about in October.

events.name: Downtown Lights
events.why: Burlington City Arts strings the winter installation through downtown and City Hall Park, and it stays up until the thaw.

events.name: Highlight — New Year's Eve
events.why: Burlington's own New Year's: art and shows all day downtown, fireworks over the lake at eight.
events.window: December 31, as it has been every year since 2018

events.name: Penguin Plunge
events.why: You run into Lake Champlain in February for Special Olympics Vermont, and then you never stop telling people.
events.window: Usually the first Saturday in February

events.name: Winter is a Drag Ball
events.why: The biggest drag night of the Vermont year, and the reason February is survivable.
events.window: Usually mid-to-late February at Higher Ground

events.name: Town Meeting Day
events.why: Vermont votes. School budgets, the city ballot, and whatever your town has been arguing about since November.

events.name: Vermont Maple Open House Weekend
events.why: Eighty-plus sugarhouses open the doors mid-boil. Free samples, steam in your face, sap on your boots.

events.name: Green Up Day
events.why: The whole state picks up the roadsides on the same Saturday. Bags are free at the town office.
events.window: The first Saturday in May, every year

events.name: Lake Monsters Home Opener
events.why: Centennial Field, cheap seats, a hill behind right field. Summer does not start until this one.

events.name: Vermont City Marathon
events.why: Twenty-six miles through the whole city on Memorial Day weekend, and half of Burlington out on the curb yelling.

events.name: Burlington Discover Jazz Festival
events.why: A week when the music spills out of the Flynn and onto Church Street, the waterfront and half the bars downtown.
events.window: Usually the first week of June

events.name: Fireworks Over the Lake
events.why: Burlington does its fireworks on the third, off the waterfront, and everyone claims a patch of grass by six.
events.window: The evening of July 3, on the waterfront

events.name: Vermont Brewers Festival
events.why: Dozens of Vermont breweries on Waterfront Park with a tasting glass and the lake in front of you.

events.name: Festival of Fools
events.why: Street performers from all over the world take Church Street for a weekend, and none of it costs anything.
events.window: Usually the end of July into early August

events.name: Lake Champlain Dragon Boat Festival
events.why: Forty-plus crews paddling off the waterfront for Dragonheart. Bring a chair; it runs all day.

events.name: Champlain Valley Fair 2027
events.why: The one that closes out every Vermont summer. Ten days, Essex Junction, and the smell of the midway.
events.window: Usually the last week of August into the first week of September
